text:
jordan: Hey — running `terraform plan` in staging and it wants to recreate namespace `payments` and the service account `payments-sa` after I updated an annotation. Plan shows replace (delete/create) for both. State seems to already have them. Anyone seen this behavior after a small annotation change? worried about breaking things :grimacing:

jordan: plan snippet:
```
# kubernetes_namespace.payments will be replaced
-/+ resource "kubernetes_namespace" "payments" {
    ~ metadata {
        - annotations = {
            - "team" = "payments"
            - } -> null
      }
  }
# kubernetes_service_account.payments-sa will be replaced
```

mina: :eyes: do you know which provider version you're on? sometimes provider upgrades change what is considered force-new.

jordan: running `terraform providers` shows `registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/kubernetes v2.11.0` (we recently bumped it in the module).

liam: ok that rings a bell — around v2.something the provider started treating some metadata changes as ForceNew in certain fields. two quick options: 1) import the existing resources into state (if the resource ids changed), or 2) add a temporary `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations] }` while we sort provider mismatch.

mina: before doing workarounds, check actual cluster state: `kubectl get ns payments -o yaml` and `kubectl get sa payments-sa -n payments -o yaml` — confirm the annotation is really different or if TF is mis-parsing.

jordan: cluster shows the new annotation is present. TF config also has the new annotation. Not sure why it wants to replace.

liam: if both config and cluster match then the problem is likely state vs provider id shape. run `terraform state show kubernetes_namespace.payments` and show the resource id. maybe the provider is serializing metadata differently.

jordan: output from `terraform state show` attached:
```
id: payments
metadata.0.annotations.%: 1
metadata.0.annotations.team: payments
```

mina: hmm state looks sane. Are you seeing any provider diagnostics in plan? like `provider changed` or `moved resource`?

jordan: plan includes this line near the top: `Warning: provider configuration not returned by provider` (something about provider schema change). Also there was a failed automated apply earlier that left a lock. When I try to `terraform apply` it errors with locked state.

ops-bot: State lock held by run CI-runner (run-2026-03-15-14:02:10). To release: `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` or wait for the run to finish.

mina: first, do not force-unlock unless you are sure the other run is stuck. Check CI job. If locked because of an ongoing run, wait. If it's stale, `terraform force-unlock` with the lock id from the error.

liam: for the recreate question: a safe path I used before — pin the kubernetes provider to the previous working version in the module, run `terraform init -upgrade=false`, then `terraform plan`. If plan no longer wants to replace, then we know it's a provider-induced ForceNew. Then either 1) roll provider forward with a migration (replace-provider or import steps), or 2) add `ignore_changes` for the annotations field and open an issue with the provider.

jordan: can we avoid downtime for the service account? If apply does delete/create will service pods lose tokens?

sre: deleting a service account can invalidate secrets/token objects bound to pods. Best to avoid actual deletion in prod. In staging you can risk it but do a staged approach: create a new SA, update workloads to use it then delete the old one. For namespace recreation it's riskier — recreating namespace deletes all namespaced resources. So we must not let terraform actually destroy the namespace.

mina: agree. so plan shows replace. If you want to unblock: add this to the resource temporarily in the TF module and run plan to confirm no replace is proposed:
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_namespace" "payments" {
  metadata {
    name = "payments"
    annotations = var.payments_annotations
  }

  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations]
  }
}
```

jordan: ok i'll try adding ignore_changes and run plan. if plan still wants replace, what next?

liam: then we may have to import the resource under the new schema or manipulate state. You can try `terraform import kubernetes_namespace.payments payments` (for the service account: `terraform import kubernetes_service_account.payments-sa payments/payments-sa`) — that will sync state to reality if TF thinks resource is missing or id changed. Always `terraform plan` after import.

jordan: import commands run, plan now shows no replace for SA but still wants to replace namespace :/

mina: check if the namespace resource has any fields marked ForceNew in the provider docs for your version. Also paste the exact diff lines from plan — sometimes it's something like `spec.finalizers` or `metadata[0].owner_references` that triggers it, not annotations.

jordan: plan diff now shows `~ metadata { - annotations = {} -> null }` (so provider thinks annotations map is being removed). We do want annotations present.

liam: sounds like a provider bug where empty maps vs null mismatch. Workaround: ensure var.payments_annotations is defined (non-empty) and matches state. Or set a default map in module so provider emits a map rather than null. Example: `annotations = length(var.annotations) > 0 ? var.annotations : {"managed-by" = "terraform"}` then adjust to real values after.

jordan: good catch. I'll set a fallback annotation so it's never null and rerun plan.

sre: also pro tip: take a snapshot of current state before doing any `force-unlock` or state edits: `terraform state pull > state-backup-$(date -u +%s).tfstate` and store it.

jordan: thanks all — adding fallback annotation fixed it, plan no longer wants to replace namespace. I'll remove the temporary annotation once we've got a clean provider migration plan.

mina: great. please also open a tiny PR documenting the provider upgrade caveat and link to the provider bug if you file one.

jordan: will do. saved the state backup and PR queued. thanks :sparkles:

liam: nice root-cause. filing a short note in infra runbook about `ignore_changes` and empty-map vs null issues would help others.

ops-bot: CI job check: the earlier lock was from run-2026-03-15-14:02:10 and has been cleared.

jordan: confirmed, apply queued and completed in staging without deleting namespace. Thanks everyone — closing the thread. :white_check_mark:
